solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Tot is covered in paper — someone very keen on hobby?

indicators.note: something covered in paper is wrapped inside it, so the paper's letters go round the rest

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
to tot up is to add
the 'is' of 'is covered in' also supplies its own letters

explanation.surface: A child gets wrapped in newspaper, while someone else obsesses over a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but here it is the verb meaning to total up. The pink-paged Financial Times is the crossword's usual 'paper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes up crazes with great enthusiasm is a follower of fads, so very keen on a hobby.

clue.text: Confounded badger involved with TB, as felt for the most part?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together
for the most part means the word felt loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A puzzled badger linked to bovine tuberculosis, with felt mostly involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confounded' could describe the badger, but it is the definition. In Britain, badgers are blamed for spreading bovine tuberculosis, which gives the surface its sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabbergasted means utterly astonished, as is someone confounded.

clue.text: The couple in wedding marched at twice the usual speed?

definitions.text: marched at twice the usual speed?

parts.note: the pair of identical letters in the word wedding are two Ds

explanation.surface: Bride and groom stride down the aisle at a gallop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The couple' looks like bride and groom, but it is the pair of letters in the middle of 'wedding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who doubled moved in double time, a quick march at twice normal pace.

clue.text: Country mist — valley regularly disappears

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words vanishes, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A countryside where fog lifts from a valley at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a European nation, a straightforward instance of a country.

clue.text: You may sit on smooth cube

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: thou is the old form of you
to sand wood is to smooth it

explanation.surface: A cube-shaped seat is offered to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten cubed, ten times ten times ten, comes to one thousand.

clue.text: Returned to make cut into beloved tree

indicators.note: cut into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: beloved means dear

indicators.note: returned means the word for 'to make' is read backwards

parts.note: to do something is to make it

explanation.surface: Someone carves into a cherished tree after coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beloved' looks like it describes the tree, but it supplies its own synonym; only 'tree' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The deodar is a Himalayan cedar, a species of large conifer.

clue.text: US city fashion associated with earlier period

indicators.note: earlier means the period's word comes first

parts.note: a day is a period of time
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: An American city's style is linked to a bygone era.
explanation.definitionFit: Dayton is a city in Ohio, birthplace of the Wright brothers' aviation work.

clue.text: Precisely where might a boxer's punch land?

definitions.meaning: exactly right, as a bet that wins outright

definitions.text: where might a boxer's punch land?
definitions.meaning: a jab to the face often hits the hooter

explanation.surface: Pinpointing where a fighter's blow lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exactly, while literally it names a target on the face for a boxer's blow.

clue.text: Notice muck on front of rotating fan

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
mire is muck or mud

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of rotating is taken

explanation.surface: A spinning electric fan gets dirt on its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' looks like a rotating machine but is a devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast, someone who looks up to and esteems another.

clue.text: A short boring article by politician full of puff?

indicators.note: short means the word for boring loses its final letter

parts.note: boring means dull
a is the indefinite article
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A brief, tedious piece by an MP turns out to be all hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Puff is extravagant praise, as in a puff piece, so writing full of it is flattering and fawning.

clue.text: Give up in retreat, set against the enemy?

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the word for give up is read in reverse

parts.note: to demit is to resign or give up an office

explanation.surface: Soldiers surrender while falling back from the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is 'the enemy' in an old saying, so something set against time is timed, as a race against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner timed by a stopwatch is measured against the clock, the proverbial enemy.

clue.text: Sonic phenomenon very loud — see troubled old pet creep around

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the musical marking
troubled means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A loud complaint about a disturbed former pet creeping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges OLD PET CREEP into DOPPLEREECT, which goes 'around' FF.
explanation.definitionFit: The change in pitch of a passing siren is this acoustic effect, named after Christian Doppler.

clue.text: Blooming friend hides behind book

indicators.note: hides behind means the friend's word is placed after the book's letter

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A pal shelters behind a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British euphemistic intensifiers, as in 'a bally nuisance' or 'a blooming nuisance'.

clue.text: Plant men round exhibition centre — prevent parking outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for preventing parking goes round the rest

parts.note: to prevent parking is to stop it

indicators.note: round means the soldiers' letters enclose the venue

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers or men
the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying out a show venue, with no cars allowed around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is a large exhibition venue near Birmingham; OR, 'other ranks', is the usual crossword shorthand for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a sedum, a low succulent often grown on walls and rockeries.

clue.text: Ease off, holding party to become reminiscent

indicators.note: holding means the word for ease off contains the other piece

parts.note: to relent is to ease off
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone calms down, throws a party, and feels nostalgic.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent that is redolent of something calls it to mind, so evocative or suggestive of it.

clue.text: Companion being entertained by former lecturer understood

indicators.note: being entertained by means the companion's letters go inside the word for former

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A guest is hosted by a retired academic who grasps things.
explanation.definitionFit: To latch on is an idiom for grasping or catching on to an idea.

clue.text: Horse is touchy coming to lake, having crossed river

indicators.note: coming to means the lake's letter follows on
having crossed means the river's letter sits across the middle of the touchy word

parts.note: to be sore is to be touchy or resentful

explanation.surface: A tetchy horse reaches a lake after fording a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorrel is a horse with a reddish-brown coat.

clue.text: They may be totally immersed in worship

definitions.text: They may be totally immersed in worship

parts.words: They may be totally immersed in worship
parts.note: deep devotion is the surface, but these believers practise baptism by full-body immersion

explanation.walkthrough: 'totally immersed' sounds like rapt devotion but is literal dunking.
explanation.definitionFit: This denomination baptises believers by full immersion in water.

clue.text: Apportions votes without leader's participation

indicators.note: without the leader taking part, the first letter of the word for votes is dropped

parts.note: ballots are votes

explanation.surface: Seats are shared out in an election the party leader sits out.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or share out, so apportions is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Plant that's dry, much withered at the sides, in shelter

indicators.note: in means the other pieces go inside the word for shelter

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
TT is teetotal, a dry drinker

indicators.note: withered at the sides means the outer letters of much fall away

explanation.surface: A plant that's parched and wilted round the edges in a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withered at the sides' leaves UC from MUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a leafy salad vegetable, so a garden plant.

clue.text: Dangerous female with long hair a terror — not half!

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word for terror is kept

parts.note: taken as the word itself, then halved

explanation.surface: A wild-haired woman is described as a terror, and how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' is also slang for 'very much so', which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is slang for a predatory woman who uses and discards lovers.

clue.text: Attempts falling short to stifle objection, producing fine words

indicators.note: to stifle means the shortened word smothers the other piece by enclosing it
falling short means the word for attempts loses its last letter

parts.note: tries are attempts
but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Failed efforts to suppress a protest yield eloquent rhetoric.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is a speech of praise, a eulogy full of admiring words.

clue.text: Guard's closer, after following

indicators.note: after means the closer's word comes behind the following letter

parts.note: an ender is something that closes or finishes

explanation.surface: A security man finishes up behind a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a protective guard, as before a fireplace or on a boat's side.

clue.text: Smallest experiment acts as setting for long one

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the experiment's word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a test is an experiment
to long for something is to itch for it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trial is set up to frame a prolonged single item.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is British slang for very small, so its superlative means smallest.

clue.text: Formal body

explanation.surface: A formal body, like a stuffy committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff means unbending in manner, and is also underworld slang for a dead body.

clue.text: Increase of sun's beginning with spring

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of sun's is taken

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Solar output rises as springtime arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger or rise, as a tide or crowd does.

clue.text: Priest and theologian admitting something little short of collapse

indicators.note: admitting means the theologian's letters let the other piece inside

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity

indicators.note: little short of means the word for collapse loses its last letter

parts.note: ruin is collapse

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a scholar take in a near-disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priest' could pair with 'theologian' as two people, but it alone is the definition; 'and' just links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A druid was a priest of the ancient Celtic religion.

clue.text: State of inactivity in man that's eaten last bit of the fat

indicators.note: a man that has eaten something has it inside him, so his word holds the rest

parts.note: dude is slang for a man

indicators.note: last bit of means the final letter of 'the' is taken

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat

explanation.surface: A man finishes off the dripping and slumps into sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Desuetude is the condition of disuse, as when a law falls into neglect.

clue.text: Note vocalist sounded

indicators.note: sounded means the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A singer hits a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music but is a banknote: a tenner is a British £10 note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is everyday British slang for a ten-pound banknote.

clue.text: Explain portion of Scripture as something that may be abused?

parts.note: to solve a mystery is to explain it
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Interpreting a passage of the Bible as a thing open to misuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Solvent abuse is the inhaling of glue or similar fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvents such as glue are notoriously misused by sniffing the fumes, hence solvent abuse.
